title: Completely useless as a shopping list
body:
This month, Google removed integration for third party list apps on Google Home devices.

This app is apparently the replacement.

It’s pathetic and does not do what I need it to do.

I have no affiliation with any app developer, but I was using an app called AnyList, and absolutely loved it. 

I could call out ‘hey google’ and add any item to my shopping list. 

The item it was automatically sorted into the correct supermarket department. (Produce, frozen, dairy, bakery - etc).

I can also add a thumbnail picture to each item if I want to, which helped ensure all family members knew which brand to buy. This is then remembered the next time the item is added.

I can also add notes to each item (quantity or any other instructions)

By stopping the (previously flawless) integration with apps like AnyList, google is trying to force me to use this pathetically excuse for an app.

It does not have the functionality I need!

Why break the integration if you can’t do it better??

Disgusting.

If there isn’t a solution found, I won’t be buying another Google product. I’ll convert our house to something that works.

title: Love this app - but please make text larger!
body:
I love this app for making grocery lists. I listed every item I ever buy according to the order of the supermarket shelves, using the tick boxes. I then ticked all items so that they dropped down below the List Items.

As I need grocery items, I touch the tick box of the item I need and it jumps up to the List Items section - AND it keeps the items in the original order. What a wonderful feature! This makes compiling my new shopping list each time so easy.

As I shop, I tick off each item, which sends it down below the List Items once again. This makes it so easy to see when I have no more shopping left to do - much better than my written lists which I would go through repeatedly to make sure I had every item. 

HOWEVER, I would love to have the option in the app of making the text larger. Then I will give it 5 stars instead of 4.

title: Version 2.2019.34: bug report + bad app + how to make it better
body:
BUGS:
Reminder notifications show up twice on my iPhone. 

When searching two terms on the Keep website, I’ll get any matching search results, but not on the iPad/iPhone app.

Both the iPhone and iPad versions crash regularly. Please fix.

PROS:
There are two display options - you can see one note under another, or they can be shown in the style of a magazine layout.

When searching, the results show up as you type.

Reminders are automatically added to Google Calendar.

You can share to it from most apps - browsers, social apps, you name it.

Just like with other Google apps, there’s no need for a “save” button on the notes because it saves everything automatically.

Add a website link and it will show a preview to remind you of what it is - very useful when you’ve got a lot of links.

Syncs perfectly between the apps on iPad, iPhone, and your browser - wherever you are, the app is always up to date.

OCR function - tap on a picture and the three dots in the top-right, and there’s an option called “Grab image text” - select that and text from the picture will be added below the picture.

Easy to move items up and down in checklists.

You can add checkboxes to a note, instantly turning it into a checklist.

No monthly limit to uploads.

Options to add colours and labels to organise notes.

When choosing between more options or more simplicity, Keep goes for simplicity.

There’s an Apple Watch app available.

Regular updates to squash bugs and improve the experience.

HOW TO MAKE IT BETTER:
Both the iPhone and iPad versions are painfully slow, especially for a Google app. If we need to delete notes to speed it up, then the app should tell us. Otherwise, remove unnecessary functions and get it moving again.

Add the ability to go straight to the top of the notes - perhaps by tapping on “Notes” in the top bar.

In the checklists, put the link previews next to the URL, instead of at the bottom of the checklist.

Remove the SAVE option on the reminders - it should save everything automatically.

Make the OCR text recognition automatic - whenever you add a picture, add any text from it below the picture.

Tapping on a link’s preview should take you to the link - the arrow icon is too small.

When a note is edited, bring it to the top - the more recent that a note is edited, the more accessible it should be.

Put info about when each note/checklist was last edited at the top so we can always see it, instead of at the bottom where it’s out of sight on long notes.

When sharing something to Keep, make it sticky by default so that it’s more accessible.

When sharing something to Keep, it would be great if the confirmation was shown for at least five seconds, so that we have enough time to choose to view the note.

When editing labels on iPhone/iPad, add the ability to swipe left to show the option to delete.

When editing a label on iPhone, prevent the “X Edit labels” from blocking us from tapping the bin icon to delete the label.

When using backspace on an item on a list, stop the cursor from continuing to delete the item above.

When adding photos to Keep, I can only do 5 at a time - increase the limit.

If a blank note or list is created, delete it automatically.

Add the option of opening links with Firefox instead of just Chrome and Safari - c’mon Google, you say that competition is good, remember?

Images added sometimes show up on their side - please fix this.

Get rid of the image-editing functions - stick to note-taking and reminders.

CONCLUSION: A bad app - it’s much too slow and crashes too often. Hopefully it’ll get fixed. If you liked this review, please long-press it and mark it as “helpful.”

title: Keep from Google is my favourite notes app
body:
Keep is like the shoebox on the end of the kitchen bench; with a PostIt note pad, a small letter pad, a to do list, shopping list, and a few reminders to pay bills. It's a staging post to something bigger (a proper document, email, or Google+ post), or the bin. 
Jot down ideas and notes to be later assembled into a memo or report. 
Use Search on label, colour, or your favourite # tag or keyword term to rapidly recover your note.
Create reminders, lists, notes; then share them.
Insert a photo of anything with text, and it will grab image text for editing.
Make a voice recording and it will grab text for editing.
Copy a note to Google Docs, or send to archive, or to bin.
Create a shared shopping list, job card, to do list, or brainstorming ideas and track each other in real time.
Measure up a job, take notes, and have staff at the workshop commence before you arrive back.
Write out a recipe and later copy it to a cooking blog, your own recipe document, share it, or chuck it in the bin.
